headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage from Khoj’s broad filesystem/network access paired with Pathway’s opaque document-processing role; other pairwise risks are low or none.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj can read indexed personal notes/files and has broad network egress, so if Pathway’s outputs are copied into Khoj or shared through files, prompt-like content could influence responses. Pathway has no filesystem read/write or network egress, so the bridge is not automatic. This is a limited, user-mediated pathway rather than a default shared channel.
conditions: IF Pathway outputs are manually pasted or saved into files that Khoj indexes
IF Khoj is pointed at a workspace containing Pathway-generated text
mitigations: Keep Pathway outputs in a separate folder not indexed by Khoj
Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted documents in Khoj
Review pasted content before placing it into Khoj
Use a read-only staging directory for Pathway exports

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents and can send data to cloud or self-hosted search providers, while Pathway is a document-processing agent with no declared data classes. The pair can therefore move sensitive documents from Khoj into a processing pipeline, creating a plausible leakage path in default use. Pathway’s lack of network egress lowers blast radius, but Khoj’s external calls keep the risk above low.
conditions: IF Khoj indexes personal notes that are then exported into Pathway workflows
IF Khoj is configured to call external search providers while processing sensitive documents
mitigations: Exclude sensitive folders from Khoj indexing
Route only redacted documents into Pathway
Disable external search providers in Khoj for sensitive sessions
Verify Pathway inputs contain no secrets before processing
Use separate storage locations for personal notes and pipeline inputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Neither agent can write the filesystem, modify git state, or use MCP, so there is no meaningful shared-write conflict. Khoj can read files and Pathway cannot, which creates asymmetry rather than contention. Any conflict would require an external orchestrator to grant both write access, which is not present in the profiles.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory
IF a separate system maps both agents onto the same mutable database or git repo
mitigations: Keep both agents on read-only mounts
Avoid shared writable workspaces
Use separate service accounts for each agent
Add file-locking in any external orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj can surface retrieved notes and documents, and Pathway is a document-processing system that may consume those outputs. If Pathway treats Khoj-generated text as authoritative, errors can cascade from retrieval into downstream processing. There is no evidence of built-in verification between them, so the safer medium rating is warranted.
conditions: IF Pathway ingests Khoj-generated summaries without validation
IF Khoj retrieval results are used as source-of-truth inputs for Pathway pipelines
mitigations: Require human review before Pathway consumes Khoj output
Add schema and provenance checks to Pathway inputs
Mark Khoj outputs as untrusted in downstream metadata
Compare retrieved facts against original documents before action

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj explicitly touches personal notes and indexed documents, while Pathway’s profile does not declare regulated data handling or residency constraints. That makes a compliance mismatch possible only if the operator routes regulated content through Pathway. Because Pathway is the only agent with no declared compliance surface, it is the relevant citation target; Khoj is cited to show the sensitive source side.
conditions: IF regulated personal data from Khoj is exported into Pathway
IF the deployment requires residency or retention guarantees that Pathway does not document
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Pathway inputs
Document retention and deletion rules before use
Use de-identified samples for Pathway testing
Confirm residency requirements are met before deployment
